headline: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff was not the original target of shooting
summary: Three suspects arrested for firing seven shots at the actor's car in Mumbai; they allegedly switched targets after finding Shroff lacked police protection.
details: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff and his driver were injured after suspects fired seven shots at his vehicle in Juhu, Mumbai, on Sunday evening.
The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the attack, stating Shroff was targeted for refusing to cut ties with Salman Khan.
Police arrested three suspects—Hrithik alias Roshan (22) and Rehan and Phool Singh (18)—who had reportedly traveled from Bihar and Haryana.
Investigations reveal the shooters were originally targeting another prominent person but switched to Shroff after tracking his movements on Instagram.
The suspects allegedly chose Shroff because fan videos showed he did not have police protection, making him an easier target.
One weapon reportedly jammed during the attack, which helped the actor and his driver escape further harm.
The accused received an upfront payment of Rs 50,000 and were promised additional money and overseas jobs.
Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited the actor on Monday and vowed to end such 'hooliganism' in the city.
caption:
Tiger Shroff was not the original target. Shooters switched to him after seeing on Instagram that he had no police protection.

Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff and his driver were injured after suspects fired seven shots at his vehicle in Juhu, Mumbai, on Sunday evening.

The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the attack, stating Shroff was targeted for refusing to cut ties with Salman Khan.

Police arrested three suspects—Hrithik alias Roshan (22) and Rehan and Phool Singh (18)—who had reportedly traveled from Bihar and Haryana.

Investigations reveal the shooters were originally targeting another prominent person but switched to Shroff after tracking his movements on Instagram.

The suspects allegedly chose Shroff because fan videos showed he did not have police protection, making him an easier target.

One weapon reportedly jammed during the attack, which helped the actor and his driver escape further harm.

The accused received an upfront payment of Rs 50,000 and were promised additional money and overseas jobs.

Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited the actor on Monday and vowed to end such 'hooliganism' in the city.

headline_marked: Rent dispute: [[AJR Courier office vandalised and looted]] in Dhaka’s Hazaribagh
headline: Rent dispute: AJR Courier office vandalised and looted in Dhaka’s Hazaribagh
summary: Masked men climbed over boundary walls to attack the warehouse, demanding rent payments to a listed criminal.
details: A group of over 100 people allegedly vandalised and looted the AJR Courier Service office and warehouse in Dhaka’s Hazaribagh on Tuesday evening.
Masked men wearing helmets climbed over the boundary wall, threatened security guards, and disabled CCTV cameras at nearby houses before the attack.
The attackers looted laptops and goods, vandalised office furniture, and removed CCTV cameras and digital video recorders (DVRs) from the premises.
The group demanded that the company pay rent for the premises to Sanzidul Islam Emon, whom police have listed as a criminal.
AJR Courier Service stated they had a lease agreement with the Sikder Group and had been paying rent to them, but attackers claimed the rent should now be paid to Emon.
Operations at the courier service have been suspended since the attack, which took place around 6:30pm near Sikder Medical College.
Hazaribagh Police Station OC Mosharraf Hossain confirmed the incident, stating that police rushed to the scene to bring the situation under control.
As of Tuesday night, no one has been detained and no formal complaint or case has been filed over the incident.
caption:
Masked men and a mob of 100+ people stormed a courier office in Dhaka, demanding rent be paid to a listed criminal.

A group of over 100 people allegedly vandalised and looted the AJR Courier Service office and warehouse in Dhaka’s Hazaribagh on Tuesday evening.

Masked men wearing helmets climbed over the boundary wall, threatened security guards, and disabled CCTV cameras at nearby houses before the attack.

The attackers looted laptops and goods, vandalised office furniture, and removed CCTV cameras and digital video recorders (DVRs) from the premises.

The group demanded that the company pay rent for the premises to Sanzidul Islam Emon, whom police have listed as a criminal.

AJR Courier Service stated they had a lease agreement with the Sikder Group and had been paying rent to them, but attackers claimed the rent should now be paid to Emon.

Operations at the courier service have been suspended since the attack, which took place around 6:30pm near Sikder Medical College.

Hazaribagh Police Station OC Mosharraf Hossain confirmed the incident, stating that police rushed to the scene to bring the situation under control.

As of Tuesday night, no one has been detained and no formal complaint or case has been filed over the incident.
